category.name: Diepe geothermie <12 MWth (basislast)
category.label: Deep geothermal, base load, under 12 MW
category.source: PBL, SDE++ 2026 advice (Lensink & Eggink, publication 5698-1, 1 July 2026), Table 11.7a p.136

notes: The plant's cost of heat has no subsidy, no tax and no sale. This is a company's view: it sells the heat and cold, gets SDE++ on its geothermal heat and pays corporate tax.
Heat is sold at 92.2 €/MWh and cold at 17.5 €/MWh: what the buyer's own gas boilers and electric chillers would cost (the 'no more than otherwise' rule of Dutch heat tariffs).
SDE++ category 'Diepe geothermie <12 MWth (basislast)' (79.9 €/MWh), chosen by the plant's geothermal capacity: 10.7 MW (300 m³/h of brine cooled 31.3 K).
Only geothermal heat earns SDE++: 58.6 GWh a year, the exchanger's heat and the heat the heat pump takes from the brine; the heat pump's electricity (5.1 GWh) and the boilers' heat earn none.

The 'high-temperature network with heat pump' categories assume the heat pump lifts all the geothermal heat, and count the heat pump's thermal output as the installation (at most that × 6,000 h is subsidised); here the heat pump only tops up after a heat exchanger, so they are not used unless you pick one.

SDE++ pays the basisbedrag less a gas-price correction (70 % of the TTF gas price, 19.6 €/MWh, at least 13.1 €/MWh), for 15 years, on at most 6,000 full-load hours a year. The CO₂ part of the correction (11.4 €/MWh) is added from year 2 (2028, when ETS2 starts). Cooling earns no SDE++.

Corporate tax 25.8 % (19 % on the first 0.2 M€ of profit a year); the plant is written off in equal parts over 15 years; losses are carried forward without the real limit. No EIA: it is not given on parts SDE++ pays for.

All money in today's euros, discounted at 5.2 % real (PBL's geothermal WACC, after tax) over 30 years. SDE++ and the tax write-offs are fixed in euros of the day, so they shrink 2 % a year in today's euros.

Units with shorter lives are bought again when they wear out; what they are still worth at the end counts back (neither taxed nor written off). Every year runs like the simulated one; the heat network is not in the plant, so not in this case.

esp._description: GEMINI's example ESP scaled to 300 m3/h (flow x1.79), 17 stages for 33 bar, power at 70% hydraulic efficiency

boiler._description: GEMINI's boiler burning the separated gas; the design's boiler is 30 MW and buys gas when the produced gas is short (the plant model)

parameters._trajectory_table_description: Cumulative MD/TVD/ID survey stations, station 0 = wellhead (MD=TVD=0); this well is fully vertical, so TVD tracks MD exactly at every station.

category.name: Diepe geothermie <12 MWth (basislast)
category.label: Deep geothermal, base load, under 12 MW
category.source: PBL, SDE++ 2026 advice (Lensink & Eggink, publication 5698-1, 1 July 2026), Table 11.7a p.136

notes: The plant's cost of heat has no subsidy, no tax and no sale. This is a company's view: it sells the heat and cold, gets SDE++ on its geothermal heat and pays corporate tax.
Heat is sold at 92.2 €/MWh and cold at 17.5 €/MWh: what the buyer's own gas boilers and electric chillers would cost (the 'no more than otherwise' rule of Dutch heat tariffs).
SDE++ category 'Diepe geothermie <12 MWth (basislast)' (79.9 €/MWh), chosen by the plant's geothermal capacity: 9.4 MW (300 m³/h of brine cooled 27.6 K).
Only geothermal heat earns SDE++: 40.2 GWh a year, the exchanger's heat and the heat the heat pump takes from the brine; the heat pump's electricity (6 GWh) and the boilers' heat earn none.

The 'high-temperature network with heat pump' categories assume the heat pump lifts all the geothermal heat, and count the heat pump's thermal output as the installation (at most that × 6,000 h is subsidised); here the heat pump only tops up after a heat exchanger, so they are not used unless you pick one.

SDE++ pays the basisbedrag less a gas-price correction (70 % of the TTF gas price, 19.6 €/MWh, at least 13.1 €/MWh), for 15 years, on at most 6,000 full-load hours a year. The CO₂ part of the correction (11.4 €/MWh) is added from year 2 (2028, when ETS2 starts). Cooling earns no SDE++.

Corporate tax 25.8 % (19 % on the first 0.2 M€ of profit a year); the plant is written off in equal parts over 15 years; losses are carried forward without the real limit. No EIA: it is not given on parts SDE++ pays for.

All money in today's euros, discounted at 5.2 % real (PBL's geothermal WACC, after tax) over 30 years. SDE++ and the tax write-offs are fixed in euros of the day, so they shrink 2 % a year in today's euros.

Units with shorter lives are bought again when they wear out; what they are still worth at the end counts back (neither taxed nor written off). Every year runs like the simulated one; the heat network is not in the plant, so not in this case.

category.name: Diepe geothermie ≥20 MWth (basislast)
category.label: Deep geothermal, base load, 20 MW or more
category.source: PBL, SDE++ 2026 advice (Lensink & Eggink, publication 5698-1, 1 July 2026), Table 11.7c p.136

notes: The plant's cost of heat has no subsidy, no tax and no sale. This is a company's view: it sells the heat and cold, gets SDE++ on its geothermal heat and pays corporate tax.
Heat is sold at 92.2 €/MWh and cold at 17.5 €/MWh: what the buyer's own gas boilers and electric chillers would cost (the 'no more than otherwise' rule of Dutch heat tariffs).
SDE++ category 'Diepe geothermie ≥20 MWth (basislast)' (62.7 €/MWh), chosen by the plant's geothermal capacity: 21.4 MW (600 m³/h of brine cooled 31.3 K).
Only geothermal heat earns SDE++: 75.2 GWh a year, the exchanger's heat and the heat the heat pump takes from the brine; the heat pump's electricity (5.2 GWh) and the boilers' heat earn none.

The 'high-temperature network with heat pump' categories assume the heat pump lifts all the geothermal heat, and count the heat pump's thermal output as the installation (at most that × 6,000 h is subsidised); here the heat pump only tops up after a heat exchanger, so they are not used unless you pick one.

SDE++ pays the basisbedrag less a gas-price correction (70 % of the TTF gas price, 19.6 €/MWh, at least 13.1 €/MWh), for 15 years, on at most 6,000 full-load hours a year. The CO₂ part of the correction (11.4 €/MWh) is added from year 2 (2028, when ETS2 starts). Cooling earns no SDE++.

Corporate tax 25.8 % (19 % on the first 0.2 M€ of profit a year); the plant is written off in equal parts over 15 years; losses are carried forward without the real limit. No EIA: it is not given on parts SDE++ pays for.

All money in today's euros, discounted at 5.2 % real (PBL's geothermal WACC, after tax) over 30 years. SDE++ and the tax write-offs are fixed in euros of the day, so they shrink 2 % a year in today's euros.

Units with shorter lives are bought again when they wear out; what they are still worth at the end counts back (neither taxed nor written off). Every year runs like the simulated one; the heat network is not in the plant, so not in this case.
